question.problem: Find the real solution to the equation $3(x+7)^{9}=1\,536.$

current_example.problem: Find the real solution to the equation $5(x-6)^7 = 640.$
current_example.worked_solution:
We can solve this equation by isolating the $(x-6)^7$ term and then taking the $7$th root of each side.

First, let's isolate the $(x-6)^7$ term on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}5(x-6)^{7} & =640 \\ (x-6)^{7} & =128\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the $7$th root of each side and solve for $x.$ Since $n=7$ is odd, there is only one real solution to this equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-6)^{7} & =128 \\ \sqrt[7]{(x-6)^{7}} & =\sqrt[7]{128} \\ x-6 & =\sqrt[7]{{2}^{7}} \\ x-6 & =2 \\ x & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=8.$
